newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds staged a modest recovery late in the session, helped by gains in U.S. and German bonds while prices of three-month futures firmed after recent sharp declines.

One trader said the market mainly watched the Swiss franc throughout the day, after the currency edged down to new lows against the mark. The mark pushed as high as 84.18 centimes, a 20-month high versus the Swiss unit, rising after a successful conclusion to Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery.
The market recovered as U.S. bonds moved higher awaiting the outcome of U.S. elections.
One Zurich-based trader said the Conf contract put on further gains when the German Bund moved above 100.00.
He said volume on the day was higher than in recent sessions, but he said the market's moves were somewhat erratic.
"You saw how quickly (the Conf contract) moved from 114.20 to 114.00. The move back up was the same," the trader said.
The drop early in the day was occured in a time span of about 10 minutes, and the move higher was similiarly abrupt.
On charts, the December confederate bond futures contract appeared to have room for further declines before year-end, but with perhaps a short-term recovery in the offing before then.

Daniel Gerber, technical analyst at CS Research, said that a roughly 38 percent Fibonacci retracement from the July low to the October high would take the Conf contract back to 113.60. A roughly 62 percent retracement would mean a pullback to 112.30.

Between those levels, a 50-percent retracment would mean a pullback to 113.00. He said a correction back to these levels was possible before the end of the year, but in the first quarter 1997, the Conf could be poised for a renewed test of roughly 116.00.
Swap rates remained volatile, but traders said they had come off their peaks by late afternoon.
Two-year swap rates had been quoted as high as 2.75/80 on Tuesday, but were back at 2.70/75 late in the afternoon, traders said.

The market was seen as still quite volatile after Swiss short-term rates rose as the Swiss franc fell on currency markets. The franc dropped steeply on Friday and Monday and continued to weaken slightly Tuesday.

Late in the day, Landwirtschaftliche Rentenbank set a 100 million Swiss franc issue with a 3-3/4 percent coupon for seven years, priced at 102.40. It was quoted late on dealers screens at a yield of 3.74 percent.
